skill.displayName: Campus Morning Brief / 校园晨报

llm.summary: This skill is a coherent student morning-brief generator with expected local rendering and no evidence of hidden execution, exfiltration, or destructive behavior.

dimensions.detail: Network research and local file output are proportionate to a current printable brief, but users should avoid placing sensitive student data in the payload.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No post-install hook, dependency installation, remote payload retrieval, or tool replacement was found; installation is documented as a normal ClawHub skill install.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The trigger language is broad and the workflow asks the agent to fetch current weather and news, but those actions are disclosed and purpose-aligned; delivery requires authorization except for established automation.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The renderer writes Markdown, HTML, and metadata files to the chosen output directory; metadata includes the profile object, including any unexpected extra profile fields supplied in input.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The instructions, references, and renderer align around generating a dated campus brief with weather, news, reminders, and printable Markdown/HTML outputs.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable with an agent researching live weather/news and saving a local brief. Use minimal student profile data, avoid sensitive schedules, health details, identifiers, or contact information, and review generated Markdown links and metadata before sharing or printing.
llm.findings:
[TP4] expected: The renderer alone does not fetch or generate current content, but SKILL.md defines an agent workflow where research happens before the local validation/rendering helper; this is a disclosed split of responsibilities, not evidence of tool poisoning.
[SQP-2] expected: Personalization by city, age group, interests, language, and reminders is core to the stated student brief purpose, though privacy guidance for minors should be made more explicit.
[LP3] expected: The skill lacks an explicit allowed-tools field, but the artifacts disclose the needed classes of activity: fetch weather/news, read supplied config, and run the local renderer.
[SQP-1] expected: The activation language is somewhat broad but stays within morning brief and student/family/class digest contexts.
[SQP-3] expected: The bilingual and zh-CN examples are visible throughout the artifact and appear to reflect the intended audience; fixed Chinese renderer labels are a localization limitation, not a security issue.
[RA2] unexpected: No cron job, plist, startup script, daemon, memory write, or other cross-session persistence mechanism was found; the cited content is age-calibration text.
[SDI-1] expected: Writing Markdown, HTML, and metadata files is disclosed in SKILL.md and README.md and is consistent with printable digest generation.
[T09] unexpected: The Markdown renderer interpolates unescaped payload text, which could allow misleading Markdown/HTML in the generated .md file if the input content is attacker-influenced; the HTML path escapes text.
[T09] unexpected: The validator preserves unknown profile fields and writes the profile to metadata.json, creating unnecessary local retention if callers include sensitive extra student data.
